label: 铁落 (tie luo, hammer-scale)

mentions.quote: raw tie luo made into a drink
Tie luo is the scaly skin

summary: Hammer-scale, entry 3812: the flakes that fly from iron heated red and forged on the anvil. The head of the entry stands on the preceding leaf, outside this book's window; this page carries its dosage, cautions, four prescriptions, commentary and Note.
canonical: 铁落 (tie luo, the scale beaten from red-hot iron; a metallurgical product, not a taxon)

label: 铁锈 (tie xiu, iron rust)

mentions.quote: Iron rust, tie xiu, is acrid

summary: Iron rust, entry 3813: the reddish-brown coat that forms on iron left exposed to the air, used against boils, mouth sores, double tongue, scabies and tinea, scalds, venomous bites and epilepsy. The entry fills the middle of this page, head to commentary.
canonical: 铁锈 (tie xiu, the rust coat of iron; a mineral product, not a taxon)

label: 铁精 (tie jing, furnace ash)

mentions.quote: Iron essence, tie jing, is a drug
Tie jing comes out of the forging hearth

summary: Iron essence, entry 3814: the ash of the iron furnace, which region 45 describes as dust-like and purple, the light sort being best. It settles fright and quiets the spirit, draws out the toxin of boils, and is used for genital swelling and rectal prolapse.
canonical: 铁精 (tie jing, the light ash of the iron-smelting furnace; a metallurgical product, not a taxon)

label: 铁马豆 (tie ma dou), the drug of entry 3815
summary: “Iron-horse bean”, entry 3815: the whole plant of the leguminous 毛宿苞豆, a Yunnan drug named by the Diannan bencao. The entry opens at the foot of the right column and runs on to the following leaf.
canonical: Shuteria vestita Wight & Arn. (the drug's one source plant, printed on this page as Shuteria pampaniniana)

label: 毛宿苞豆 (mao su bao dou), printed as Shuteria pampaniniana
summary: Hairy shuteria, the leguminous climber that is the sole botanical source of 铁马豆; the 原植物 line naming it is the last text on the page.

label: 甘草 (gan cao)
summary: Liquorice, the second ingredient of the mania prescriptions of both 铁落 (region 4 ②) and 铁精 (region 42 ①).
canonical: 甘草 (liquorice root, Glycyrrhiza; species not stated here)

label: 蒜 (suan, garlic)
summary: Garlic, ground with 铁锈 and applied for the bites of spiders and other insects (region 15) and for those of the earwig and the centipede (region 20).
canonical: 蒜 (garlic, Allium sativum; the page names only the drug)

label: 冰片 (bing pian, borneol)
summary: Borneol, ground with 铁锈 in water for prolapse of the uterus after childbirth (region 20), and one ingredient of the secret boil-drawing powder of region 26, where it is named by the single character 脑.
canonical: 冰片 (borneol, a crystalline plant exudate; source species not stated)

label: 青竹 (qing zhu, green bamboo)

mentions.quote: burn green bamboo for its oil

summary: Green bamboo, burnt for its oil and rubbed on together with 铁锈 for the sores of scalds and burns (region 25 ⑤).
canonical: 青竹 (green bamboo; genus not stated)

label: 《本草汇言》 (Bencao huiyan)

mentions.quote: Collected Sayings on Materia Medica [Bencao huiyan]

summary: Collected Sayings on Materia Medica, cited six times here, as often as the Benjing fengyuan and oftener than any other work: the caution and the thief-wind prescription of 铁落, the boil-toxin actions of 铁锈, and the flavour, the action and the long commentary of 铁精.

label: 《本经逢原》 (Benjing fengyuan)

mentions.quote: Encountering the Source of the Classic of Materia Medica [Benjing fengyuan]

summary: Encountering the Source of the Classic of Materia Medica, quoted six times here — for the caution on 铁落, the flavour and two uses of 铁锈, and the slight poison, the action and the warning commentary of 铁精.

label: 《素问》 (Suwen)
summary: The Basic Questions of the Yellow Emperor's Inner Canon, credited in region 4 with the Raw Iron-flake Drink and invoked again in the commentary of region 5 as the warrant for it.

label: 《方脉正宗》 (Fangmai zhengzong)

mentions.quote: Orthodox Lineage of Prescriptions and Pulses [Fangmai zhengzong]

summary: Orthodox Lineage of Prescriptions and Pulses, source of prescription ② of 铁落, for sudden rage breaking out into mania.

label: 《千金方》 (Qianjin fang)
summary: The Thousand Gold Pieces Prescriptions, source of prescription ④ of 铁落, copper and iron dross in lard for mottled erysipelas in children.

label: 《本草经疏》 (Bencao jingshu)

mentions.quote: Commentary on the Classic of Materia Medica [Bencao jingshu]

summary: Commentary on the Classic of Materia Medica, which supplies the whole 各家论述 of 铁落 (region 5) and of 铁锈 (region 26) and the first flavour reading of 铁锈.

label: 《本经》 (Benjing)

mentions.quote: Classic of Materia Medica [Shennong bencao jing]

summary: The Classic of Materia Medica, the Han root text of the tradition: the naming source of entry 3814 铁精 and the authority quoted for its neutral nature and for brightening the eyes.

label: 《唐本草》 (Tang bencao)

mentions.quote: Materia Medica of the Tang [Tang bencao]

summary: Materia Medica of the Tang, whose long quotation forms the whole 备考 of 铁落 and defines the drug as the smith's scale rather than iron liquor.

label: 《甲乙》 (Jiayi)

mentions.quote: the Jiayi, i.e. the Systematic Classic of Acupuncture and Moxibustion [Zhenjiu jiayi jing]

summary: The Jiayi, cited inside the Tang bencao quotation as the place where 铁落 is spoken of, in the section on yang reversal in the zi fascicle.

label: 《本草拾遗》 (Bencao shiyi)
summary: The naming source of entry 3813 铁锈 and the first authority quoted for its actions, against malign sores, scabies, tinea and the bites of spiders.

label: 《普济方》 (Puji fang)
summary: Prescriptions for Universal Relief, cited for the synonym 铁衣 and as the source of the first two 铁锈 prescriptions, the calcined rusty nail and the boil powder mixed with human milk.

label: 《养生经验合集》 (Yangsheng jingyan heji)

mentions.quote: Collected Experiences in Nourishing Life [Yangsheng jingyan heji]

summary: Collected Experiences in Nourishing Life, cited for the second synonym of 铁锈, 铁线粉 “iron-wire powder”.

label: 《日华子本草》 (Rihuazi bencao)
summary: Rihuazi's Materia Medica, the sole authority for the preparation of 铁锈 and the source of its epilepsy, heart-settling and hair-blackening uses.

label: 《本草经解》 (Bencao jingjie)

mentions.quote: Explanation of the Classic of Materia Medica [Bencao jingjie]

summary: Explanation of the Classic of Materia Medica, the one authority given for the channels entered by 铁锈, the hand taiyin lung and the foot yangming stomach.

label: 陶华 (Tao Hua)
summary: Ming physician of Yuhang in Zhejiang (1369-1463), the best-known cold-damage specialist of his generation, whose name stands on this page in the slot where the dictionary otherwise prints a book title.
canonical: 陶华 (Tao Hua), zi Shangwen, hao Jie'an, 1369-1463

label: 《纲目》 (Gangmu)

mentions.quote: The Gangmu, i.e. the Compendium of Materia Medica [Bencao gangmu]

summary: The Gangmu, quoted for the liver-calming and sore-dispersing action of 铁锈 and cited for the synonym 铁花 of 铁精.

label: 《嘉祐方》 (Jiayou fang)
summary: The Jiayou Prescriptions, cited inside the Bencao huiyan quotation of region 19 for grinding 铁锈 into the Chengqi decoction in cold damage with heat-repletion binding in the chest.

label: 《医林纂要》 (Yilin zuanyao)

mentions.quote: Essentials Compiled from the Forest of Medicine [Yilin zuanyao]

summary: Essentials Compiled from the Forest of Medicine, quoted for the heart-supplementing action of 铁锈 and for the lung-draining, phlegm-felling action of 铁精.

label: 《圣济方》 (Shengji fang)
summary: The Sagely Benefaction Prescriptions, source of prescription ③ of 铁锈, rust water for the red roving wind of the legs.

label: 《生生编》 (Shengsheng bian)

mentions.quote: the Compilation on Fostering Life [Shengsheng bian]

summary: The Compilation on Fostering Life, source of prescription ④ of 铁锈, rust knocked from a heated lock for double tongue.

label: 《积德堂经验方》 (Jidetang jingyan fang)

mentions.quote: the Tried Prescriptions of the Hall of Accumulated Virtue [Jidetang jingyan fang]

summary: The Tried Prescriptions of the Hall of Accumulated Virtue, source of prescription ⑤ of 铁锈, bamboo oil and rust for scalds and burns.

label: 《濒湖集简方》 (Binhu jijian fang)

mentions.quote: Binhu's Collected Simple Prescriptions [Binhu jijian fang]

summary: Binhu's Collected Simple Prescriptions, source of prescription ⑥ of 铁锈, rust ground in water for wind-itch and nettle rash.

label: 《活人心统》 (Huoren xintong)

mentions.quote: the Comprehensive Guide to Saving Lives [Huoren xintong]

summary: The Comprehensive Guide to Saving Lives, source of prescription ⑦ of 铁锈, powdered rust taken in cold water for seminal emission from internal heat.

label: 《子母秘录》 (Zimu milu)

mentions.quote: Secret Records of Mother and Child [Zimu milu]

summary: Secret Records of Mother and Child, cited for the synonym 铁精粉 and as the source of prescription ② of 铁精, powdered iron essence dusted on genital swelling.

label: 《别录》 (Bielu)
summary: The Supplementary Records, quoted for the slightly warm nature of 铁精 and for the fullest statement of its indications, fright palpitation, wind epilepsy in children, genital swelling and rectal prolapse.

label: 《至宝方》 (Zhibao fang)
summary: The Supreme Treasure Prescriptions, source of prescription ① of 铁精, iron essence with liquorice for fire-heat scorching the heart.

label: 《圣惠方》 (Shenghui fang)
summary: The Sagely Benevolence Prescriptions, source of prescription ③ of 铁精, the mutton-fat compress ironed on for uterine prolapse.

label: 姚和众 (Yao Hezhong)
summary: A Tang writer on children's ailments, dates unknown, named in person — with no book attached — as the source of prescription ④ of 铁精, powdered iron essence dusted on a child's prolapsed rectum after dysentery.
canonical: 姚和众 (Yao Hezhong), Tang author on the ailments of children, dates unknown

label: 《补缺肘后方》 (Buque zhouhou fang)

mentions.quote: the Supplemented Handy Prescriptions for Emergencies [Buque zhouhou fang]

summary: The Supplemented Handy Prescriptions for Emergencies, source of prescription ⑤ of 铁精, blown through a tube into a wound pricked by a snake's bone.

label: 陶弘景 (Tao Hongjing)
summary: Daoist scholar, alchemist and pharmacologist of the Southern Dynasties (456-536), founder of the Shangqing lineage and the man who put the received materia medica in order; he is named on this page as a person, not through a book.
canonical: 陶弘景 (Tao Hongjing), zi Tongming, the Recluse of Huayang, 456-536

label: 《滇南本草》 (Diannan bencao)

mentions.quote: Materia Medica of Southern Yunnan [Diannan bencao]

summary: Materia Medica of Southern Yunnan, the naming source of entry 3815 铁马豆 and of its synonym 黄花马豆.

label: 《昆明民间常用草药》 (Kunming minjian changyong caoyao)

mentions.quote: Common Folk Herbal Medicines of Kunming [Kunming minjian changyong caoyao]

summary: Common Folk Herbal Medicines of Kunming, cited for the second synonym of 铁马豆, 蝴蝶草 “butterfly herb”.
canonical: 《昆明民间常用草药》 (Kunming minjian changyong caoyao)

label: Handel-Mazzetti (Hand.-Mazz.)
summary: Austrian botanist (1882-1940), collector and monographer of the flora of southwest China, whose standard abbreviation Hand.-Mazz. is the authority of the binomial with which this page ends.
